---
title: "Threshold Model for Binary Traits"
---

## TL;DR

::: {.callout-tip}
A binary trait (disease, mortality, fertility) is modelled as the
result of an **unobserved continuous liability** $\ell$ crossing a
threshold. The mixed model is fit on the liability scale, and the
observed 0/1 outcomes constrain $\ell$ through a probit (or logit)
link. `masreml` uses a **single-step Laplace approximation** so the
solve is direct and roughly as fast as the continuous case.
:::

## The model

Each individual $i$ has a latent liability

$$
\ell_i = \mathbf{x}_i^\top \mathbf{b} + \mathbf{z}_i^\top \mathbf{u} + \varepsilon_i,
\qquad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0, 1),
$$ {#eq-liability}

and the observed binary response is

$$
y_i = \mathbb{1}\bigl[\ell_i > 0\bigr].
$$ {#eq-threshold}

The unit residual variance is a convention (probit link); under logit
it becomes $\pi^2 / 3$. The random additive genetic effects have the
same prior structure as the continuous case:
$\mathbf{u} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{K}\sigma_u^2)$, with
$\mathbf{K}$ the relationship matrix of choice
(see [GBLUP & GWABLUP](gblup-gwablup.qmd)).

Heritability on the **liability scale** is

$$
h_\ell^2 = \frac{\sigma_u^2}{\sigma_u^2 + 1}.
$$ {#eq-h2-liability}

Heritability on the **observed (0/1) scale** depends on prevalence $K$:

$$
h_{\text{obs}}^2 = h_\ell^2 \cdot \frac{z(K)^2}{K(1-K)},
$$ {#eq-h2-observed}

where $z(K) = \phi(\Phi^{-1}(K))$ with $\phi$, $\Phi$ the standard
normal density and CDF. Use @eq-h2-observed when reporting
heritability for case-control samples whose prevalence differs from the
population.

## Estimation in `masreml`

Direct Gibbs sampling of $\ell$ is slow because each individual's
liability must be redrawn from a truncated normal at each iteration.
`masreml::masreml(y, markers = ..., trait = "binary", link = "logit")`
instead uses a **single-step Laplace approximation** (also referred to
as a Gaussian approximation on the liability scale in
`R/binary.R`):

1. From the observed prevalence, build a working response $z_i$ on the
   liability scale via Fisher-scoring with the chosen link.
2. Solve the linear MME (see [Mixed Models & BLUP](mixed-models-blup.qmd#eq-mme))
   for the working response, re-estimating $\sigma_u^2$ via REML.
3. Iterate the working response until convergence.

This is equivalent to a generalized linear mixed model fit via
penalized quasi-likelihood (PQL) — fast and accurate when the liability
variance is moderate. For very low prevalence (e.g. rare disease) a
full MCMC sampler is more robust; `link = "probit"` and `link = "logit"`
are both available — probit matches the liability-scale derivation
exactly, logit is slightly more numerically stable.

## Assumptions

1. **Liability is normally distributed.** A probit link encodes this
   directly. Logit-link estimates are close in practice but assume a
   slightly leptokurtic liability.
2. **Threshold is fixed at zero** (after absorbing the intercept into
   $\mathbf{b}$).
3. **Same random-effect structure as the continuous model** — wrong
   $\mathbf{K}$ biases the estimated heritability and breeding values
   the same way it does for continuous traits.
4. **No ascertainment correction** is automatic. If your sample is
   case-enriched (case-control prevalence $\neq$ population
   prevalence), the intercept and variance components need a
   Falconer-Lush adjustment before back-transforming to the observed
   scale.

## Calibration metrics

Predictive accuracy on a binary trait is **not** $r(\hat{u}, y)$ —
that statistic conflates discrimination with prevalence. Report
instead:

| Metric | What it measures |
|---|---|
| Liability-scale $r(\hat{\ell}, \ell_{\text{true}})$ | Discrimination on the latent scale (simulation only) |
| AUC | Discrimination on observed 0/1 |
| Brier score | Calibration + discrimination jointly |
| Calibration slope of $\hat{p}_i$ against $y_i$ | Pure calibration; should be 1 if perfectly calibrated |

`masreml::evaluate_prediction()` reports AUC and Brier; the
calibration slope is a one-line `glm(y ~ phat, family = binomial)`.

## When to use

| Outcome type | Use this model |
|---|---|
| Continuous trait | Standard mixed model — see [Mixed Models & BLUP](mixed-models-blup.qmd) |
| Binary, common (5–50% prevalence) | Threshold model with Laplace approximation (`masreml(y, markers = ..., trait = "binary", link = "logit")`) |
| Binary, rare (< 1% prevalence) | Threshold model with full MCMC sampler; or a logistic GBLUP on the case-only subset |
| Multi-category ordered (e.g. severity 1–4) | Cumulative-link threshold — not yet implemented in `masreml`; collapse to binary as a workaround |
